claims.text: The investigated particles are sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles synthesized by pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane.
The as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles initially have an FCC structure.
The initial nanoparticles are compositionally homogeneous in their bulk.
Edges, vertices, and other coordination defects in sub-5 nm particles lower the activation barrier for element-specific surface diffusion.
Surface-energy minimization gradients, rather than configurational-entropy stabilization, dominate segregation and evaporation in sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt particles.
Au and Cu are low-cohesive-energy or low-surface-energy constituents that preferentially segregate to the nanoparticle surface.
In sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt particles, the reduction in surface free energy from Au/Cu segregation outweighs bulk configurational-entropy stabilization.
The surface-energy imbalance drives rapid surface diffusion and evaporation of Au and Cu.
Surface diffusion and evaporation cause elliptical particles to become spherical and reduce particle size.
The proposed surface-mediated pathway bypasses the sluggish diffusion associated with bulk high-entropy alloys.
Au/Cu segregation and evaporation accelerate near a critical temperature of approximately 600–700 K.
Above the critical temperature, Au/Cu segregation and evaporation rates increase exponentially.
Preferential evaporation of the smallest particles produces measurable mass loss and narrows the particle-size distribution.
After segregation and evaporation, the remaining particle core preserves its FCC structure while its shell is depleted in Au and Cu.
Configurational entropy can stabilize a single-phase structure in a multicomponent material.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion stabilize FCC AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles against coalescence and segregation up to temperatures near constituent melting points.
The proposed mechanism applies strictly to particles smaller than 10 nm and depends on their initial shape.
Truncated-octahedral particles dominated by low-surface-energy {111} facets should segregate less than icosahedral particles.
Particles larger than 50 nm should exhibit negligible segregation and remain stable to higher temperatures.
Surface-energy terms dominate the configurational-entropy term in sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says preferential loss of the smallest particles will narrow the size distribution, whereas the motivating observation states that heating widens the size distribution.
